answer.rationale: The two live deficits are onboarding completion (-4% QoQ) and activation (-6% QoQ), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a fix there can propagate to both. Two independent inherited records (memory_31 signup-field reduction, memory_86 shortened onboarding) point the same way, which is stronger convergent support than the single activation-messaging record (memory_91). The competitor's entry pricing creates obvious pressure toward promotional_pricing, but memory_73 is the one memory with hard numbers and it shows the trade explicitly: signup +31% and revenue +18% bought at -12pp monthly retention. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is a negative-value trade, and matching a competitor on price also concedes the dimension we compete worst on. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is credible but does not address the SMB-side deficits that are actually moving. Referral incentives (memory_57) act on established customers and will not repair a leaking top of funnel. I am spending verification on the two memories that underwrite the action I intend rather than on memory_73, which is already specific enough to act against. Both memory_86 and memory_31 are stated in proxy terms ('completion rates', 'first-week activation', 'durable lift') with no mention of retention, revenue, or lead quality; I want the source records to tell me whether the lift was ever traced past the proxy and over what horizon 'durable' was measured. The live downstream risk: stripping signup fields and onboarding steps can raise completion while degrading lead qualification data and admitting lower-intent accounts, so raw completion could improve while qualified revenue flattens or falls. I will therefore run this with a holdout and hold retention, downstream conversion, and revenue-per-signup as guardrails rather than treating completion as the success metric. If verification shows either record measured only proxies, I will narrow to a small guarded test before any broad rollout.
